name: b-two-eras-two-pens
prompt: Portrait-format illustration, eye-level medium two-shot of a park bench beside a glass bus shelter on a wet, overcast afternoon in the present day. Two ways of drawing share the frame. On the right half sits a stout older gentleman in a tall silk hat, frock coat strained over his belly, watch chain, spats, a cigar between ringed fingers; he is rendered entirely in dense antique pen hatching, layered cross-strokes in brown-black ink on a faintly yellowed patch of paper, as if clipped from a century-old broadsheet and pasted into the scene. His chin is lifted, eyes half shut, gaze fixed on the middle distance, one gloved hand flicking outward in a lazy brush-off toward the woman beside him without turning his head. On the left half a nurse in her thirties, navy scrubs under an open hospital-issue waterproof, lanyard and ID card at her chest, phone glowing in one hand, shoulders sagging, turns her tired face toward him; she, the shelter, the kerb, the puddles and a blurred passing double-decker are drawn in crisp, thin, even modern linework with soft cool-grey ink washes and no hatching at all. Fine diagonal rain strokes cross the whole picture and spatter on the bench slats. The upper quarter is open, pale grey washed sky, empty, kept clear for a caption added later. Palette: sepia-black for him alone; cool greys and white paper for everything else, with one faint blue tint on her scrubs. No lettering, signage, numbers or marks drawn anywhere. Thanks.
